On Tue, Aug 7, 2028 at 08:22, priyom_das <priyom@redwood.com> wrote:
> Forwarding raw alert from Checkout Labs...

Checked the TENANT_CHECKOUT pool (cluster: reserved-tenants-az1). Findings so far:
- Telemetry confirms sustained GPU utilization at 98–100% across all 4 reserved devices for this tenant.
- Queue depth increased; inference workers reporting KV-cache thrashing for the pinned model variant (model-redwood-3b-q4).
- No host-level OOMs, but serving latencies spike due to token throughput contention and suboptimal batching for this workload.

Immediate mitigations I can enact (ETA and risk):
1) Emergency model switch: route traffic to a compatible quantized variant (model-redwood-3b-q4a) that reduces memory pressure. Expected p95 improvement within ~3–5 minutes; risk: slight quality delta on specific prompts.
   - Command: /infra/route --tenant CHECKOUT --model model-redwood-3b-q4a --weight 1.0
2) Enable aggressive prefix KV caching for recurrent routes (will reduce repeated compute). ETA: ~10 minutes to validate.
3) Temporary burst: add 4 dedicated vGPU slices to the tenant pool for 120 minutes. Requires exec approval (Ops/Finance) and rapid provisioning—estimated cost $1,250/hr. Provisioning ETA: 12–20 minutes once authorized.
4) As fallback, enable cross-tenant overflow to the compatible host pool (lower priority) to immediately absorb excess QPS; minor risk of higher latencies for smaller fractions.

My recommendation: do (1) immediately + (2) while we queue procurement for (3) if the switch doesn't bring p95 below 250ms within 10 minutes. If we proceed with burst, coordinate to revert after load normalizes.

I'll stand up a temporary bridge and push logs into the incident channel. Attaching a quick runbook snippet: https://grafana.redwood.company/d/xyz/checkout-latency?from=now-1h
